strings.name: David Solomon
strings.role: Goldman Sachs Chairman and Chief Executive Officer
strings.summary: David Solomon is an American investment banker who joined Goldman Sachs as a partner in 1999, later leading investment banking and becoming president and an operating chief. He became CEO in 2018 and chairman in 2019; his responsibilities span capital markets, asset management, risk and accountability in a large financial institution.
strings.coverageNote: Checked through November 17, 2026, including the October 13 results and interview transcript published October 27. Recording and publication dates, corporate results and personal wealth, and institutional legal resolutions and individual responsibility are distinguished.
strings.influence.rationale: Leads Goldman Sachs' investment banking and asset management businesses, participating in global capital markets and corporate financing.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: He earned a Hamilton College bachelor's degree in 1984; the college calls the major Government and Goldman Sachs calls it Political Science. These refer to the political-science field, not two degrees.
strings.facts.f2.label: Educational governance
strings.facts.f2.value: He chairs Hamilton College's Board of Trustees; this is a governance role, not the college presidency.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Institutional accountability
strings.highlights.h1.text: In the 2020 1MDB resolution, Goldman Sachs' parent entered a deferred prosecution agreement and its Malaysian subsidiary pleaded guilty. The board separately reduced current executives' combined compensation by $31 million; this was not Solomon's personal fine or conviction.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Responsibility for AI deployment
strings.highlights.h2.text: In a 2026 interview he advocated shared AI-governance responsibility among governments, model developers and deploying companies. His optimism about jobs acknowledged near-term disruption and represents an opinion, not a proven outcome.
strings.timeline.t1.title: AI and jobs interview published
strings.timeline.t1.text: The transcript dates the recording to October 26; it discusses technology adoption and human accountability, without treating forecasts as realized benefits.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Third-quarter results released
strings.timeline.t2.text: Goldman Sachs reported net revenues of $18.68 billion and net earnings of $5.29 billion for the quarter ended September 30; these are corporate figures.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Addresses institutional accountability over 1MDB
strings.timeline.t3.text: After the legal and regulatory resolutions were announced, Solomon discussed accountability and improved controls in a staff message, while the board adjusted executive compensation.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Adds Goldman Sachs chairmanship
strings.timeline.t4.text: Already CEO, he took over the board chairmanship; the two roles did not begin on the same date.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Becomes Goldman Sachs CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: He succeeded Lloyd Blankfein and joined the board; the succession had been announced on July 17.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes president and co-COO
strings.timeline.t6.text: He moved from investment banking management to firmwide operations; the 2016 appointment announcement is distinct from starting the role in 2017.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Becomes investment banking co-head
strings.timeline.t7.text: He jointly led the Investment Banking Division, not the entire company as sole CEO.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joins Goldman Sachs as a partner
strings.timeline.t8.text: He had previously worked at Irving Trust, Drexel Burnham and Bear Stearns.
